sentences.text: In view of the averments made in the affidavit filed in support of the application, the application is allowed.

The order dated 11.7.2019 is recalled in the light of order dated 16.11.2020 passed by the Apex Court in Criminal Appeal Nos. 750-751 of 2020 arising out of SLP (Crl) Nos. 4292-4293 of 2020 (Parveen vs. State of Haryana) and the Criminal Revision is restored to its original number.
Order on memo of revision Supplementary affidavit filed today be taken on record.
Heard learned counsel for the revisionists and learned A.G.A. for the State.

As per office report dated 5.4.2014, revisionist No. 1-Gyan Das son of Shyam Lal died, therefore,
present criminal revision is abated against revisionist No. 1.

The present revision has been preferred against the judgment and order dated 19.08.1988 passed by Ist Additional Sessions Judge in Criminal Appeal No. 100 of 1995, dismissing it and confirming the order dated 18.10.1985 passed by Special Judicial Magistrate (Economic Offences), Basti convicting the appellants under Sections 7/16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration in Criminal Case No. 1055 of 1984 and sentencing two years R.I. and fine of Rs. 2,000/- and in default of payment six months R.I and the applicants have been further convicted for offence punishable under Section 7/16 (1) A 1(II)
for Prevention of Food Adulteration Act for two months R.I. and fine of 3,000/- and in default of payment of fine 15 days R.I.
Learned counsel for the revisionists at the very outset stated that he is not assailing judgment of the Courts below on merits, but is seeking mercy stating that this is an old matter.

The accused-revisionist no.2 are now attained advance age and also undergone the sentence around 8 months, therefore, sentence of imprisonment awarded to them be reduced to the period already undergone.

Looking to the entire facts and circumstances and considering this fact that except this case revisionist no.1 is having no criminal history, while maintaining the conviction, I am inclined to reduce sentence of imprisonment to the period already undergone though a fine of Rs. 2000/- each is imposed against revisionist No.2.
Accordingly, Revision in respect of Revisionist no.2 is partly allowed.

Conviction of accused-revisionist no.2 is maintained, but, sentence awarded by Trial Court under Sections 7/16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration is modified and reduced to the extent of sentence of imprisonment already undergone by accused-revisionist no.2 though a fine of Rs. 2000/- is imposed.
The revisionist no.2 be released from jail forthwith subject to deposit of fine of Rs. 2000/-, in case earlier not deposited.
Certify the judgment to the Court below immediately.

Order Date :- 19.3.2021 Junaid  Gyan Dass And Others vs State on 19 March, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41871032/
